headline_marked: [[Buyer context significantly shifts]] AI product recommendations, moving 6 of top 10 results in one market.
headline: Buyer context significantly shifts AI product recommendations, moving 6 of top 10 results in one market.
summary: Adding specific buyer situations to AI recommendation queries drastically reorders product suggestions, displacing top incumbents and surfacing entirely new product categories previously unmentioned.
details: An experiment testing AI answer engines (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) revealed that adding specific buyer context to product recommendation queries significantly alters results. In one market, 6 of the top 10 recommended products shifted, and 4 in an unrelated market.

The methodology involved asking AI engines 44 variations of a buying question, then counting named products. A control run confirmed the top ten remained identical without context changes, isolating the effect to the added buyer information.

Initially, for a CRM market, a product went from 0 mentions in 132 answers to 83, becoming first in its category after context was added. This displaced the previous leader, HubSpot CRM, which finished 4th.

The effect was reproduced in an unrelated call center software market. A pre-selected product moved from being unmentioned to within the top 15 of 127 distinct products named when context was provided.

The added context not only reordered existing recommendations but also introduced a significant number of new products. The CRM run surfaced 113 products with context vs. 65 without, with only 25 in common.

In the call center market, 127 distinct products were named with context compared to 75 without, with 88 products appearing that generic questions never surfaced. This included a coherent class of self-hosted telephony stacks and on-premise solutions from major incumbents.

This suggests that adding buyer context primarily opens categories to product classes that generic questions cannot reach. The extent to which these new classes dominate the top recommendations varies by market.

The study also highlights a disagreement among AI engines regarding how much a buyer's stated constraints should influence the answer. For example, ChatGPT moved a tracked product to 11 of 44 questions, while Perplexity moved it to 0.

headline_marked: [[Google Messages fixes two annoying quirks]] with new long-press menu and selective copy
headline: Google Messages fixes two annoying quirks with new long-press menu and selective copy
summary: The latest Google Messages beta introduces a revamped long-press menu for easier access to actions and the ability to selectively copy parts of a message, improving the overall texting experience.
details: Google Messages is finally addressing two long-standing user frustrations: the inability to selectively copy text and a cumbersome long-press menu. These much-needed changes are rolling out in the latest beta update.

Previously, the long-press menu scattered actions like copy, delete, and forward across a top toolbar and an overflow menu. This made common tasks like sharing or forwarding messages unnecessarily complicated for users.

The revamped long-press menu now consolidates all key actions—Reply, Forward, Copy, Star, Delete, Select more, Info, and Save—into a single, polished menu. This eliminates the need for the top toolbar and three-dot menu, streamlining the user experience.

Additionally, users can now long-press a chat again to select and copy only specific parts of a message. Previously, Google Messages only allowed copying the entire text of a message, a basic function that has been missing for a long time.

These features have been in testing for several months, with the new long-press menu first spotted almost a year ago. While neither feature is groundbreaking, together they significantly enhance the app's usability by reducing taps and making frequently used actions more accessible.

Currently, these upgrades are only available to select users on the beta channel. Google is expected to push these improvements to the stable version of Messages soon, bringing a better experience to all users.
